title: Complete and Partial Bell Polynomials at Bernoulli Numbers and Other Sequences, with Applications to Multiple Zeta Values
content: Comparing the Maclaurin series of a function with that of its logarithm or exponential yields closed-form values of the complete Bell polynomials. Combining this principle with the Faà di Bruno formula and Newton's forward differences, the author evaluates the complete and partial Bell polynomials at sequences built from the Bernoulli numbers, eta and zeta values, factorials, and Stirling, harmonic, and Catalan numbers, and at the Maclaurin coefficients of logarithms of several elementary functions. The main new results concern products of sine and hyperbolic sine functions, which involve the Bernoulli numbers B4k, and exponentials of six elementary functions. The radius of convergence of the series of \( \bigl(\frac{\tan z}{z}\bigr)^\lambda \) is determined for every real λ. As applications, the author derives a convolution identity for B4k, closed forms and monotonicity of the multiple zeta values \( \zeta(4,4,\dotsc,4) \) and \( \zeta^*(4,4,\dotsc,4) \) , and Ramanujan-type evaluations of series involving \( \frac1{\sinh(\pi m)} \).
